messages.subject: grsmIRT
parts:
Hi Phill,

I am trying to fit a grsmIRT model. However, I am getting the message:

> gradedmod <- mirt(Answer, 1, 'grsmIRT', technical = list(removeEmptyRows=TRUE))

Error: Rating scale models require items to have the same number of categories

All items, though, are rating from 1 to 5. I do have some no responses, but I don't think this is the problems. If you could help me figure it out, I would much appreciate it.

Thank you,

Juliane

messages.author: 70d0917afd869432
messages.subject: Re: grsmIRT
parts:
Hi Juliane,

I believe that error means you have some questions where not all responses (the 1-5s) are used.  If you search the forum, I think Phil has provided some solutions to account for this issue in the past.

Best,
Matt

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Re: grsmIRT
parts:
Collapse some categories (1 & 2 → 2) or try this. it needs psych()

Seongho


# a part of https://github.com/seonghobae/k.aefa/blob/master/k.aefa3.R
x <- data.frame(x)
if(length(which(psych::describe(x)$max > median(psych::describe(x)$max))) != 0){ # preventing weird input (e.g: 6 in 5 point scale)
for(ii in which(psych::describe(x)$max > median(psych::describe(x)$max))){
x[,ii] <- mapvalues(x[,ii], describe(x[,which(psych::describe(x)$max > median(psych::describe(x)$max))])$max, NA)
}
}
x <- x[,which(psych::describe(x)$range == max(psych::describe(x)$range))] # delete items which have non-equal number of categories
k <- vector()
for(iii in 1:length(x)){
for(j in range(na.omit(x[iii]))[1]:range(na.omit(x[iii]))[2]){
if((sum(na.omit(x[iii]) == j) == 0) == TRUE){
k[length(k)+1] <- colnames(x[iii])
}
}
}
x <- (x[,!colnames(x) %in% k])
for(iiii in 1:ncol(x)){
x[,iiii] <- as.integer(x[,iiii])
}
message('\nMIRT model: graded rating scale')
try(modTEMP <- mirt::mirt(data = x, model = i, itemtype = 'grsmIRT', method = estimationMETHOD, accelerate = accelerateINPUT, calcNull = T, technical = list(symmetric_SEM = symmetric_SEMINPUT, SEtol = SEtolINPUT, removeEmptyRows = T), TOL = TOLINPUT, covdata = covdataINPUT, formula = formulaINPUT, optimizer = optimINPUT, solnp_args = optimCTRL, SE = SE, SE.type = SE.type, ...), silent = F)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: grsmIRT
parts:
Seongho is probably right that the best strategy is to simply collapse categories, or perhaps not use the rating scale models at all (they rarely fit well anyway). 

That being said, you can hack at some of the code by including survey weights for arbitrary response patterns to trick the program into thinking that categories exist when they really don't. This might have unforeseen consequences in secondary functions, but for model comparison reasons it's fine. See below.

library(mirt)

dat <- Science
dat[,2] <- dat[,2] + 1
dat[,3] <- dat[,3] + 2
dat[,4] <- dat[,4] + 2
lapply(dat, table)
 
dummy <- matrix(min(dat):max(dat), nrow=6, ncol=4) 
colnames(dummy) <- colnames(dat)

w <- c(rep(0, 6), rep(1, nrow(dat)))
mod <- mirt(rbind(dummy, dat), 1, 'grsmIRT', survey.weights = w)
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE)

plot(mod, type = 'trace')

itemfit(mod)
personfit(mod)
fscores(mod)


Phil
